summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for progressive dyspnea and productive cough over three weeks, consistent with mucus accumulation due to recurrent tracheal stenosis from relapsing polychondritis and SMAD4 syndrome. He had missed a scheduled bronchoscopy and presented with increased yellow tracheal secretions. He underwent flexible bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and both main bronchi, which relieved his symptoms. Bronchial washings grew Klebsiella oxytoca, prompting a seven-day course of cefpodoxime. A CT chest showed stable airway stenosis and no acute findings despite transient desaturation with ambulation. His white blood cell count improved from 14.0 to 10.7, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, continue baseline medications, and follow up with interventional pulmonology and primary care.
